65834bea23a0.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About the OS Integration team:

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, updater, and enterprise DLP support. 

About the role:

As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. In many cases work may be cross-platform or have a cross-platform component. This role will include maintenance and development of the installer and updater of Firefox. You’ll contribute to the team through code review and discussion.

What you’ll do: 

  • Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users.
  • Contribute to new features and improvements.
  • Break down tasks and work with others to deliver solutions.
  • Collaborate with experienced software engineers.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is working on frontier AI systems that handle sensitive information at enormous scale. How we protect that data, and how we build privacy into our systems rather than bolting it on afterward, is central to our mission of building AI that is safe and beneficial.

As one of our principal privacy engineers, you will be among Anthropic's most senior individual contributors on privacy. You will set technical strategy for how personal data is handled across products, research, and infrastructure, and execute the hardest parts of delivering it. You'll work at the intersection of privacy engineering, distributed systems, and AI safety, on problems without established answers. You will lead through influence, quality of thinking, and trust rather than formal authority.

  • Turn regulatory, contractual, and consent obligations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, the EU AI Act) into enforced, continuously verified technical controls in partnership with Legal, Policy, and Compliance team
  • Anticipate where AI capabilities, regulation, and customer expectations are heading, and position our systems ahead of them
  • Mentor and develop staff and senior staff engineers, raise the bar for privacy design across engineering, and help hire senior privacy talent
  • Represent Anthropic's privacy engineering to customers, regulators, standards bodies, and the research community

Minimum qualifications

  • A track record of operating as a Principal engineer or equivalent: setting technical direction that multiple teams adopted, and delivering company-critical, multi-year initiatives
  • Deep experience applying privacy engineering principles in production systems with a large user base, including privacy by design, data minimization, and purpose limitation

ac65c8f34436.description:
HackerRank helps companies like NVIDIA, Amazon, and Microsoft hire and upskill the next generation of developers based on skills, not pedigree. Our platform is trusted by over 2,500 of the world’s most innovative companies to build strong engineering teams ready for what’s next.

Software has entered an era where humans and AI build side by side. As this shift accelerates, the definition of strong technical talent is changing. We give companies better ways to identify and invest in next-generation skills.

People at HackerRank care deeply about the impact of their work and sweat the small details so our customers can be wildly successful with products they genuinely love to use. We move with urgency and believe great outcomes come from high standards.

Open Problems

The agentic era is reshaping every layer of the hiring stack. These are some of the core problems you'll be working across, none of them fully solved.

  • Chakra: Building an autonomous AI interviewer that conducts, adapts to, and evaluates technical interviews end to end.

  • Translate cutting-edge research into scalable, production-grade AI systems.

Who you are

  • M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D. in AI/ML or related disciplines.
  • 3-7 years of experience in Deep Learning, Machine Learning, or Applied AI Research.

You will build and own high-throughput backend services in Go that ingest device telemetry through AWS IoT and Kinesis, process it in real time, and land it in Redshift for analytics and reporting. Your systems have to handle spikes without losing a single event, scale without anyone stepping in, and stay cheap enough to run at volume. This is a senior, hands-on engineering role. You make sure the data that lands is correct, complete, and ready for analytics. Own reliability and cost: You build monitoring, alerting, and dashboards across the pipeline with CloudWatch or similar tools, and you track latency, data loss, and AWS spend. You know the cost per million events and how to bring it down. Raise the engineering bar: You lead design discussions, review code, write clear technical documents, and mentor other engineers on the team.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Anthropic grows, more of the work our own teams do every day runs through internal software, and that software has to keep up. We are building that software, and we are building it Claude-first: Claude should take on as much of the repetitive, multi-step work as it safely can, and people decide what needs a human.

We’re looking for Staff+ full-stack engineers to drive this work. You’ll build across the stack: the products people use and the agents that work alongside them. You’ll work directly with the teams who rely on what you build. Many of these workflows write to business-critical data, so correctness matters as much as speed.

This is a greenfield opportunity: you’ll shape the underlying systems, ship agents that take real work off people’s plates, and design how people and agents get the right context to make good decisions.

Key responsibilities

  • Design and ship internal products end to end, from the data model to the UI, for workflows that teams across Anthropic depend on.

  • Integrate with the third-party systems teams already rely on, and build the layer on top of them where people and agents get their work done.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

About the Team & Impact
At Okta, Demo Engineering bridges the gap between product innovation and go-to-market execution—acting as a global force multiplier for our technical sales organization. We equip internal and partner Solution Engineers worldwide with the tools and environments needed to effortlessly demonstrate how Okta secures identities across workforces, customers, and AI agents.

In this role, your code directly powers Okta’s global sales engine. The demo architectures and interactive experiences you create will be leveraged by hundreds of field engineers across dozens of countries, influencing thousands of enterprise customer conversations. Operating within an engineering-first, collaborative culture focused on automation, modularity, and self-service, you will build the core platform that makes Okta’s field teams faster, sharper, and more scalable.

What You’ll Do

  • Architect Reusable Assets: Design and develop modular demo components and pre-configured product environments tailored to high-impact, solution-driven customer scenarios.
  • Capture Field Insights: Partner closely with global field teams to gather "Voice of the Customer" feedback—translating prospect expectations, preferences, and friction points into platform improvements.
  • Drive Platform Adoption: Team up with Field Readiness to champion the Demo Platform and accelerate usage across the broader go-to-market organization.
  • Measure & Optimize: Build telemetry, analytics, and reporting dashboards to monitor demo engagement and quantify field impact.
  • Launch New Capabilities: Collaborate cross-functionally with Product Management and Core Engineering to build demo-ready experiences ahead of new product releases.
  • Influence Product Roadmap: Represent field and customer insights during release planning to help shape future product direction.
  • Enable the Field: Author clear technical walkthroughs, demonstration guides, and video tutorials to empower self-service adoption.

What You Bring to the Table

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

bf0a38a99cb9.title: Senior Data Scientist, Trust (ML/Algo)
bf0a38a99cb9.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

“Our real innovation is not allowing people to book a home; it’s designing a framework to allow millions of people to trust one another. Trust is the real energy source that drives Airbnb…” 

- Brian Chesky, Airbnb Co-Founder & CEO (2019)

Trust is the foundation of a vibrant Airbnb community. The Trust Integrity Data Science team helps build and protect that trust by ensuring that the content on Airbnb, including listings, profiles, messages and other user-generated experiences, is accurate, authentic and aligned with our policies and community standards.

We partner closely with product, engineering, policy and operations teams to develop advanced AI-driven content understanding systems, scale effective human-in-the-loop workflows and proactively defend against emerging content risks, so guests and hosts can interact with confidence.

The Difference You Will Make:

This role sits at the heart of some of Airbnb's most consequential data science challenges, where rigorous statistical thinking and applied ML directly shape platform outcomes. You will own high-visibility initiatives that require both technical depth and strong business judgment - work that is visible to leadership and has measurable impact on Airbnb's users and bottom line.

The ideal candidate is a motivated and talented Data Scientist with strong applied machine learning intuition, a bias toward impact and the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive clarity in complex problem spaces.

A Typical Day: 

  • Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning: Build and deploy production AI/ML systems for trust integrity, including feature engineering, model development and evaluation, thresholding, error analysis and end-to-end model lifecycle management. This includes working with NLP and LLM-based models in real production settings.
  • Inference: Partner with inference data scientists to conduct rigorous quantitative analyses, applying working knowledge of causal inference to interpret results, assess impact, and identify gaps and opportunities to improve content quality and trust

About The Company:
At Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business. A leader in autonomous driving since 2007, Torc has spent over a decade commercializing our solutions with experienced partners. Now a part of the Daimler Truck family, we are focused solely on developing software for automated trucks to transform how the world moves freight. Join us and catapult your career with the company that helped pioneer autonomous technology, and the first AV software company with the vision to partner directly with a truck manufacturer.

Meet The Team:
Torc is hiring a Senior Systems Engineer to own the safety concept, safety architecture, and safety case for autonomous vehicles that operate in unstructured, off-highway environments. Our team adapts Torc’s L4 autonomy stack to specialty vehicle platforms and delivers them to customers for hands-on evaluation. We are a small, dedicated group that owns the system end to end, from hazard analysis through on-vehicle verification, and we work directly with vehicle manufacturers, suppliers, and Torc’s corporate safety organization.

What You’ll Do:
This role is focused on the safety of autonomous ground vehicles in unstructured environments: defining what “safe” means for each platform and use case, designing the safety architecture that achieves it, and producing the evidence that it has been achieved. In a secondary capacity you will contribute to the system architecture of the autonomy kit itself, so that the safety concept holds across multiple vehicle platforms and generations of compute. You will work closely with systems, software, controls, perception, hardware, and test engineers, and you will be the second independent safety voice on a lean team.

  • Safety Engineering
    • Lead hazard analyses for new platforms and use cases, and derive safety goals and functional safety requirements from them.
    • Perform single-point-failure and fault-tree analyses of the autonomy system, including compute, sensing, communications, and drive-by-wire paths, and define fault detection, degraded modes, and minimum-risk maneuver behavior.
    • Define the safety requirements and acceptance criteria for partner-supplied drive-by-wire and emergency-stop systems, and lead their integration assessment.
    • Build and maintain structured safety cases (for example, GSN) for successive operating phases: closed-course testing with a safety driver, remote operation, and customer-operated evaluation.
    • Prepare and present safety assessments to internal safety governance boards and to customer and partner reviews, and act as an independent safety reviewer in the software and hardware release process.
  • Safety and Systems Architecture
    • Define the safety-relevant interfaces of the au

Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.

We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.

Job Description

Join Olsson’s Data Center Mechanical Design team as a Fire Protection Engineer, where you’ll take the lead on complex, mission-critical projects, including hyperscale data centers and secure facilities. This is a highly visible role within a multidisciplinary team known for delivering innovative, high-performance building systems.

You’ll provide technical leadership on fire protection strategies that safeguard infrastructure, protect assets, and meet the most rigorous code and client requirements. You’ll collaborate with architects, MEP engineers, and security professionals across sectors such as data centers, healthcare, higher education, commercial, industrial and federal facilities.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead the design and execution of fire protection systems for secure and mission-critical facilities
  • Develop and review fire suppression, alarm, and life safety system designs to meet client and code requirements (NFPA, IBC, IFC, UFCs, etc.)
  • Serve as the technical expert and client liaison for fire protection scopes on data center and secure facility projects
  • Coordinate across disciplines to ensure fully integrated system design
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to internal knowledge-sharing
  • Support proposal development and contribute to project scope and scheduling
  • Occasionally travel to project sites or other Olsson offices as needed (approximately 15–25%)

You are passionate about:

  • Working collaboratively with others.
  • Having ownership in the work you do.
  • Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

Build the Path Forward

At Path Robotics, we’re building the future of embodied intelligence. Our AI-driven systems enable robots to adapt, learn, and perform in the real world closing the skilled labor gap and transforming industries. We go beyond traditional methods, combining perception, reasoning, and control to deliver field-ready AI that is risk-aware, reliable, and continuously improving through real-world use.

Big, hard problems are our everyday work, and our team of intelligent, humble, and driven people make the impossible possible together.

We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Robotics team. You'll use machine learning to improve how our robots plan, scan, and act. You'll frame real robot problems as well-defined ML problems, train models on data that a fleet of production robotic cells generates every day, and ship them into a production stack where they work alongside classical planning and perception. Your models run on live robots doing real work for customers.

What You'll Do

  • Frame open-ended problems in planning, scanning, and robot behavior as well-defined ML problems.
  • Train models that work with classical methods, such as initial guesses and learned costs for trajectory optimization, plan quality and feasibility predictors, and learned collision models.
  • Develop viewpoint planning policies that choose where and how to scan, and predict scan quality before the robot commits.
  • Apply imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and generative models such as diffusion and flow matching where they outperform classical baselines.
  • Build production ML pipelines: datasets from fleet logs and simulation, training, and metrics.
  • Evaluate models in the loop, with offline metrics that predict gains on the robot, failure-mode analysis, and calibrated confidence that determines when the system falls back to classical methods.
  • Own your models end to end, from prototype to deployment on live robotic cells, with low-latency inference and monitoring.

Who You Are

  • An MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of applied machine learning for robotics or autonomy, in research or industry.
  • Fluent in Python with PyTorch or JAX, and experienced training, evaluating, and deploying deep learning models.
  • Strong foundations in linear algebra, 3D geometry, kinematics, and optimization.
  • You've run your methods on real robot hardware.
  • You explain model results and their limits clearly, so planning, perception, and field teams know when to trust them.

Preferred
